title: Embed traffic governor: cumulative quality-lag fence for staged model swaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Prior embedding model swaps have produced transient semantic regressions that only appear after accumulating traffic across multiple tenants and query cohorts. We need an automated guard that gates incremental traffic to new embedding variants based on both immediate signal (semantic-delta on eval set) and a running cumulative quality-lag measurement on production cohorts.

Goal: Implement a traffic governor service + integration in the embed gateway that enforces a cumulative quality-lag fence during staged model adoption and deprecation. The governor should combine cohort-level rolling quality delta, token-latency budgets, and a small cohort-specific rollback window to automatically slow, pause, or roll back swaps when cumulative quality degradation exceeds thresholds. This should support multi-variant (A/B/n) swaps, tenant pinning, and opt-out for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private.
acceptance_criteria: A governor service exists that receives per-cohort quality deltas and exposes a decision API (allow/slow/pause/rollback)
Embed gateway integrates governor and honors decisions within 2s of API response for new requests
Cohort-level telemetry shows rolling 24h and 7d cumulative quality-lag metrics for any active swap
Automated canary that ramps to 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% per policy unless governor pauses/rolls back
Runbook created for manual intervention and rollback with links to dashboards and tenant impacts
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests for governor logic; shadow mode in staging
Phase 1: Shadowing in prod for 2 weeks (no traffic control) — collect cohort deltas and false-positive analysis
Phase 2: Soft-control canary on 3 internal tenants (5% traffic) with automatic slow decisions enabled
Phase 3: Wider canary to 20% across mixed cohorts with rollback automation enabled for high-severity regressions
Phase 4: Default policy for public swaps; opt-outs for Dedicated/Private customers via console flag
telemetry_metrics: p99_request_latency_ms: target < 120ms impact from governor interactions
implementation_notes: Core components: lightweight governor service (Go), inference-side adapter in embed gateway, cohort prober job that runs semantic checks per tenant, and a small datastore for swap state. Use existing telemetry exporters and augment with a per-swap UUID. Keep decision rules declarative so PMs can tune. Leverage token-bucket throttling in gateway to implement 'slow' decisions rather than immediate drop. Persist swap audit trail for forensics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Governor introduces latency to request path — Mitigation: cache decisions for 5s and use async fetch; keep decision API sub-10ms in prod region
Risk: False positives block healthy swaps — Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, shadow validation for 2 weeks, and disable rule for known low-volume tenants
Risk: Cohort definition drift causes noisy signals — Mitigation: cohort-prober periodically revalidates sampling and falls back to tenant-level aggregation
Risk: Ops burden for manual rollbacks — Mitigation: build single-click rollback in Console with pre-computed impact estimate
decisions: Decision: Use cumulative 7-day window + short 24-hour sensitivity to balance long-tail regressions and early detection
Decision: Implement 'slow' as token-bucket-based partial throttling rather than uniform probability sampling
Decision: Store swap state in the existing embed-meta table (extend schema) for consistency with rollout tooling
Decision: Default policies run on Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can opt-out per contract
qa_and_evals: Create a curated eval set that mirrors critical enterprise prompts (privacy-preserving) for the prober
Run synthetic perturbation tests to validate governor triggers under controlled regressions
Smoke-test latency impact across regions with quantized variants enabled
